sections.markdown:
**Think of Scandit as the industrial-grade, paid-tier scanner used by real warehouses.**

`mobile_scanner` is the free / open-source option — great for QR + basic retail. Scandit is what UPS drivers, Amazon warehouse pickers, and pharmaceutical logistics use. Its CV models handle:

- **Damaged codes** — creased, scratched, faded 1D codes that ML Kit fails on.
- **Small codes at distance** — reading a Code 128 label 2 meters away.
- **Multi-code capture (MatrixScan)** — scan 10 codes on a shelf simultaneously with AR-style overlay.
- **Text + barcode combined** — read a VIN + barcode, or price tag OCR + barcode in one frame.
- **Extreme lighting** — direct sunlight, shadows, glare on packaging.

Both technical advantage AND commercial support — SLA-backed license, guaranteed accuracy on damaged codes tested at customer sites.

**Why enterprises pay for it:** in a warehouse where a scan retry costs $0.05 (worker time), a 5-point accuracy improvement at scale pays for the license. Free scanners work fine for consumer QR; Scandit shines when scanning is the primary business flow.

**Scandit SDK** is a commercial computer-vision SDK specializing in barcode + text + ID capture. **Products** include: **Barcode Capture** (single/multi barcode), **MatrixScan** (AR overlay + multi-code), **ID Capture** (drivers licenses, passports), **Label Capture** (text + barcode combos), **SparkScan** (in-app scan button). Flutter access via `scandit_flutter_datacapture_barcode`, `_id`, `_label`, `_core` packages. Requires a license key (per-app + per-feature); free trial + community license for < 25 devices.

## Common mistakes
**Mistake 1: Hardcoded license in source.** Someone grabs it from the APK + your license usage explodes. Store in a build-time config; rotate periodically; per-env keys.
**Mistake 2: Enabling every symbology.** Slower detection + more CPU. Restrict to what you actually scan (e.g., Code 128 + EAN for retail).
**Mistake 3: Ignoring `codeDuplicateFilter`.** Same code fires repeatedly in continuous mode; Scandit's filter prevents this.
**Mistake 4: Not disposing camera / context.** Native memory leak. Switch camera off + release.
**Mistake 5: Ignoring license expiry.** Trial licenses expire; production apps hard-fail. Wire monitoring.
**Mistake 6: Testing only on Pixel + iPhone Pro.** Cheap Android hardware behaves differently; test on Redmi / Realme / entry-level iOS.
**Mistake 7: MatrixScan without dedup logic.** Multi-code capture returns codes many times per frame; app-level Set-based dedup by (code + session) needed.
**Mistake 8: No offline fallback.** License activation on first launch checks Scandit servers; if offline + license unactivated, scanner won't start. Cache activation.
## Best practices
**1. License in secure build config** — never in git.
**2. Narrow symbology list.**
**3. `codeDuplicateFilter`** for continuous mode.
**4. Test on entry-level hardware.**
**5. MatrixScan for warehouse — dedup via Set.**
**6. Label Capture for text + barcode** — cleaner than roll-your-own.
**7. Monitor license usage** in Scandit dashboard.
**8. Fallback to mobile_scanner** for QA / dev builds without Scandit license.
## Practice programs
**Practice 1 (Easy)** — Basic single-scan with community license (<25 devices).
**Practice 2 (Medium)** — Multi-format scan + haptic + de-dup filter.
**Practice 3 (Medium)** — MatrixScan overlay showing multiple detected codes at once.
**Practice 4 (Hard)** — Label Capture: scan price tag showing text + barcode together.
**Practice 5 (Hard)** — Warehouse app: session-based inventory list with Wi-Fi outbox sync.
**Practice 6 (Expert)** — Feature-flag Scandit vs mobile_scanner at runtime; measure accuracy delta on 50 damaged codes.
## Interview Q&A

**Q1: Why would a company pay for Scandit when free options exist?**

**A:** **Accuracy delta on damaged / low-light / distant codes.** In a warehouse where each scan retry costs 3-5 seconds of worker time × millions of scans per year, a 5-10 % accuracy improvement pays the license fee 10-fold. **Also:** MatrixScan (10 codes simultaneously with AR overlay — impossible with mobile_scanner); Label Capture (text + barcode combined — clean SDK vs roll-your-own); ID Capture (parse driver's licenses / passports — regulatory sensitive); enterprise SLA + support; on-device training data curated by Scandit's team. **When free is fine:** consumer QR scanning, occasional retail lookup — free options suffice. **Trade-offs:** cost (~$5-20 per device / year at scale), APK bloat (~10-20 MB per Scandit product), license lifecycle (rotation, monitoring). Interviewer signal: pragmatic 'pay when the ROI justifies it.'

**Q2: How does Scandit handle multi-code capture (MatrixScan) that mobile_scanner cannot?**

**A:** MatrixScan continuously runs Scandit's CV pipeline on every camera frame + emits ALL detected codes with their bounding boxes + tracking IDs. UI overlays a colored rectangle around each detected code + tracks them across frames (like an AR game). **Use case:** scanning 20 items on a shelf simultaneously — user hovers the phone; UI shows each item highlighted; tap to confirm add-to-inventory. **Under the hood:** proprietary tracking algorithm + dedup filter + optimized detection cascade that returns multiple codes per frame. **Free scanners can't do this well** because ML Kit returns detections per frame without tracking; you'd have to hand-roll persistence + dedup + overlay. **Business value:** a warehouse picker scans 30 % faster with MatrixScan vs one-at-a-time. Retail scanners in stock rooms use it for shelf audits.

**Q3: How do you manage the license lifecycle?**

**A:** **(1) Never in git.** Store in a build-time config (`--dart-define`); different keys per env (dev, staging, prod). **(2) Rotate periodically** — quarterly at least; if a leak is suspected, immediately. **(3) Scandit dashboard shows usage** — # devices, activated features, per-day scans. Alert on anomalies (leaked key = spike in unfamiliar device IDs). **(4) License expiry monitoring** — trial keys have deadlines; enterprise keys renew annually. Wire alerts. **(5) Feature-flag** — some Scandit products (ID Capture, MatrixScan) require separate license entitlements. Ensure your license covers the features your app uses. **(6) Offline behavior** — first-launch activation contacts Scandit servers; if offline + never activated, scan fails. Cache activation after first success; test in airplane mode. **(7) Cost tracking** — Scandit bills per device-year at scale; budget accordingly.

**Q4: How would you architect a warehouse app using Scandit?**

**A:** **(1) Session state** — one session = one warehouse task (e.g., picking a specific order). Persist in Hive / drift so a crash mid-shift doesn't lose scans. **(2) Symbology restriction** — Code 128 + Code 39 + EAN-13 depending on the warehouse standard; skip QR. **(3) MatrixScan for shelf audits** — AR overlay + tap-to-confirm. **(4) SparkScan for hands-free continuous scan** — floating scan button that stays on top even while browsing the picking list. **(5) Offline outbox** — every scan writes to local DB + queues for upload via Workmanager. **(6) Audio + haptic feedback** — user's eyes are on the item, not the phone. **(7) Bar-code-to-item catalog** locally so instant lookup even offline. **(8) Analytics on retry rate** — track scan-fail per code type + measure Scandit vs baseline. This is the textbook enterprise warehouse architecture.

**Q5: When would you NOT use Scandit?**

**A:** **(1) Consumer QR-only app** — mobile_scanner is fine + free. **(2) Small pilot / prototype** — trial license OK but avoid infrastructure commitment. **(3) Free tier < 25 devices** — Scandit's community license covers it; still evaluate free options first. **(4) Simple retail POS with lots of well-printed codes** — accuracy delta doesn't justify cost. **(5) Regulated pharma or medical apps requiring specific certifications** — verify Scandit's compliance matches; sometimes specialty SDKs win. **(6) When APK size is tight** — Scandit adds 10-20 MB per product; consumer app budget may not allow. **(7) When ML Kit + custom-tuning suffices** — some teams squeeze accuracy from free options with camera-controlled lighting + overlays. **Interview red flag:** 'always Scandit for scanning' — nuance matters.

**Q6: How do you test Scandit-backed code?**

**A:** **Unit tests** — abstract behind a `ScannerService` interface; production impl = Scandit; test impl = fakes. Assert on business logic (dedup, session, outbox), not on Scandit internals. **Integration tests** on real hardware — Scandit provides sample PDFs of damaged codes for regression testing; print + scan periodically. **CI:** don't test the SDK in cloud CI (no camera); test business layer. **Manual regression** on new Flutter or SDK version — Scandit updates the CV models regularly; run through your damaged-code test set. **A/B compare** — feature flag Scandit vs baseline scanner in beta; measure retry rate + user complaints. **Load / stress** — MatrixScan on a shelf of 30 codes; verify frame-rate holds + no memory leak. Interviewers respect the 'business layer over SDK internals' answer.

## Real-world usage

- **Enterprise warehouses** — UPS, DHL, Amazon.
- **Retail** — inventory audits + POS.
- **Pharmaceutical** — GS1 DataMatrix with damaged / small codes.
- **Airline / hospitality** — boarding passes + ID capture at check-in.
- **Field service** — asset tags + serial number capture in dim environments.
- **NOT ideal for** — consumer QR-only apps; sub-25-device deployments (community license fine but why bother if not enterprise features).

## Advanced notes

- **SparkScan** — pre-built in-app scan button; drop-in scanning UX.
- **ID Capture** — parses MRZ + PDF417 on driver's licenses + passports.
- **Label Capture** — combines OCR + barcode; e.g., price tag showing SKU + name + price.
- **Feedback Bindings** — sound + vibration + LED customization per event.
- **Camera zoom + focus** — Scandit auto-controls; can override.
- **Custom UI overlays** — draw your own bounding boxes via BarcodeCaptureOverlay customization.
- **Progressive licensing** — start with Barcode Capture; upgrade to Matrix + ID as needs grow.
- **Text Capture** — pure OCR for VINs, price tags, IBAN numbers.
- **Scandit Cloud (enterprise)** — usage analytics, license portal, remote config for scanner settings.
- **iOS + Android parity** — well-tested but occasional platform-specific bugs; report to Scandit support.
- **Version bumps** — SDK updates often need re-license activation; test upgrade path.
- **Deprecation cycle** — Scandit deprecates OS versions over time; check minimum iOS + Android targets.
